sdk.title: SDK Reference
sdk.description: Build Nostr apps with data fetchers, relay utilities, login UI, and optional follow-graph distance queries.
sdk.packagesDescription: Versions verified on npm on 20 September 2026. The meta-package exposes WoT at its root and other modules through subpaths. You can also install scoped packages directly; @nostr-wot/pq is a separate package.
sdk.setupDescription: NostrSdkProvider composes data configuration, session state, and optional WoT context. Supply myPubkey explicitly for Oracle queries; signing in does not set the WoT query root automatically.
sdk.dataDescription: Standalone fetchers retrieve profiles, notes, threads, follows, and engagement. React hooks add a cache with stale-while-revalidate behavior. Data fetchers share their own connection pool.
sdk.relayDescription: RelayPool wraps a compatible PoolLike transport supplied by your app. Configure urls, use subscribe with onEvent/onEose, and close subscriptions when finished. A separately created relay wrapper is not automatically connected to the data provider.
sdk.uiDescription: LoginButton and useSession share the session provided by NostrSdkProvider. Supported methods include NIP-07, NIP-46, key generation, and key import. Install the UI package directly when importing its components and styles.
sdk.wotDescription: WoT queries the Oracle by default. getDistance returns a number or null; isInMyWoT returns a boolean. getDetails provides hops, a numeric path count, and optional bridges and mutual-follow information. Pass valid 64-character hexadecimal public keys.
sdk.migrationDescription: Version 1.0.0 removed browser-extension detection, trust-score methods, and useTrustScore. Use useWoT or useIsInWoT and read their result objects. For local queries, pass a WoTLocalSource, such as WotGraph.asWoTSource() from @nostr-wot/graph. Only getDistance, isInMyWoT, and filterByWoT use that source; other methods still query the Oracle.
sdk.compatibilityDescription: Published @nostr-wot/wot 1.0.0 uses the older /api/distance/FROM/TO?maxHops= contract and expects a distance field. Oracle 0.3.0 uses /distance?from=&to=&max_hops= and returns hops. Changing the base URL alone does not make them compatible. Use direct fetch for Oracle 0.3.0, or the local graph source shown below.
sdk.localDescription: Load and crawl a local graph before passing its source to WoT. The React example receives this prepared graph and uses useIsInWoT; useWoT also requests getDetails from the Oracle. @nostr-wot/graph has its own getScore API, separate from the removed WoT score API.

extensionApi.title: Extension API
extensionApi.metaDescription: NIP-07 signer API reference for the Nostr WoT browser extension: identity, event signing, relay settings, encryption and request failures.
extensionApi.intro: The extension exposes <api>window.nostr</api> for identity, event signing, and NIP-04/NIP-44 message encryption.
extensionApi.prerequisite: Install the <download>extension</download>, select an account, and connect your site when prompted. Signing and encryption require a signing-capable account and may prompt you to unlock the vault. Reading a known public key does not require unlocking it.
extensionApi.setupDescription: Check for the method you need before calling it. An injected provider does not mean the site is connected or a request has been approved.
extensionApi.name: Name
extensionApi.standard: The extension implements the <standard>NIP-07 signer API</standard> exposed through <api>window.nostr</api>.
extensionApi.getPublicKey: Returns the active account's hex-encoded public key. Requires site connection and identity access.
extensionApi.signEvent: Signs the event and adds id, pubkey and sig. Supply created_at yourself; the signer preserves your timestamp. If you supply pubkey, it must match the active account. Signing does not publish the event.
extensionApi.event: Event containing kind, content, tags and created_at (Unix time in seconds)
extensionApi.nip04Encrypt: Encrypts a message using NIP-04, the legacy direct-message encryption format.
extensionApi.nip44Encrypt: Encrypts a message using NIP-44. This example uses the standard two-argument call.
extensionApi.getRelays: Returns the relay URLs configured in the extension. Each entry has read: true and write: true. This method does not fetch the account's NIP-65 relay policies and may return an empty object.
extensionApi.errorsDescription: Calls return Promises and can reject if the user declines, the site is disconnected, identity access is disabled, or the request times out. Signing and encryption are unavailable for read-only accounts.
extensionApi.errorsDetails: An account switch can invalidate a pending request. Page calls time out after 120 seconds, including time spent waiting for connection, permission or unlock. Catch errors and let the user retry; error messages are not stable machine-readable codes.
extensionApi.trustRedirect: Use the <sdk>SDK</sdk> for follow-graph queries and the <oracle>WoT Oracle API</oracle> for public mute evidence. Mute evidence is separate from follow distance; it does not produce a combined trust score. The extension provides identity and signing.

integration.extensionDescription: Browser identity, event signing and encryption through window.nostr.
integration.oracleDescription: For server-side apps. No user extension required. Use our public server or self-host.
integration.sdkDescription: TypeScript packages for Nostr data, relays, login and local graph queries. Check the API compatibility notes before using remote WoT queries.
integration.exampleDescription: Query the Oracle v0.3.0 API directly. Replace these example keys with your own 64-character hexadecimal pubkeys:

start.intro: Get up and running with Web of Trust in just a few minutes.
start.queryTitle: Query the Oracle from a browser or server
start.queryDescription: Oracle v0.3.0 supports standard fetch requests. Use full 64-character hexadecimal public keys. No extension or SDK is required.
start.hopsDescription: Hop values: 0 = yourself, 1 = direct follow, 2 = follow of follow. A null result means no path was found within the requested depth in the indexed graph. Coverage depends on the configured relays. The extension provides signing and identity; it does not answer graph queries.
start.serverDescription: For server-side applications, use the Oracle REST API. No extension required.
start.mutesDescription: Follow distance and public kind-10000 mute observations are separate evidence. The API does not combine them into a numeric score or decrypt private mute entries. Unknown mute lists and lists with no public entries are different states. Define your application's policy explicitly.
start.compatibilityDescription: Published @nostr-wot/wot@1.0.0 uses legacy remote endpoints and response fields that Oracle v0.3.0 does not expose. Remote SDK distance queries can report null after a 404, so do not interpret that as a verified graph result. Use the fetch examples above for this Oracle.
start.sdkDescription: The SDK's data, relay and identity packages remain useful independently. For local graph queries and React integration, see the verified SDK examples. useTrustScore is not part of the published WoT 1.0 API.

oracleApi.distanceKeys: from and to: required source and target pubkeys.
oracleApi.includeBridges: include_bridges: boolean, default false. Includes search meeting nodes when available.
oracleApi.bypassCache: bypass_cache: boolean, default false. Recomputes from the current indexed graph; does not fetch new relay data.
oracleApi.pagination: Required pubkey; optional offset (default 0) and limit (default 500, capped at 5000). total is the full indexed list size, independent of the page size.
oracleApi.title: Oracle API
oracleApi.intro: Version 0.3.0: directed follow distance and separate public mute evidence over HTTP. No extension required.
oracleApi.baseUrl: Base URL: <link0>https://wot-oracle.mappingbitcoin.com</link0>. No API key is required by the Oracle.
oracleApi.requestFormat: Send pubkeys as full 64-character lowercase hexadecimal strings, not npubs. The examples use synthetic pubkeys to illustrate response shapes; your graph results will differ. POST requests use Content-Type: application/json.
oracleApi.rootDescription: The root endpoint GET / lists the service version, documentation and available endpoints. For your own instance, see the self-hosting guide.
oracleApi.distanceEvidence: Distances use directed kind-3 follow edges. Public kind-10000 mute lists are separate observations. The Oracle does not combine them into a trust score or remove muted accounts from follow paths.
oracleApi.healthReadiness: A healthy process can still be waiting for relay events or unable to persist updates. Use /ready for ingestion readiness.
oracleApi.readyDescription: Ingestion snapshot: HTTP 200 when ready, HTTP 503 otherwise.
oracleApi.readyDetails: Readiness requires running ingestion, no current database failure and a follow or mute event received within five minutes. A quiet private relay can therefore yield 503 even while the process is operational. Example while waiting for the first event:
oracleApi.timestamps: Timestamps are Unix seconds, with zero meaning not yet observed. persisted_events counts accepted author updates written to storage after batch coalescing. lagged_notifications and persistence_errors expose ingestion problems.
oracleApi.statsDescription: Indexed graph counts, cache settings, lock metrics and ingestion status.
oracleApi.statsDetails: Counts and settings above are illustrative. edge_count counts follow edges; mute_edge_count counts public pubkey mute edges. nodes_with_mute_lists includes known lists with no public pubkey entries. Lock timings are in microseconds. The sync object has the same fields as /ready.
oracleApi.distanceDescription: Shortest directed follow distance from one pubkey to another.
oracleApi.distanceResult: hops is zero for self-distance and one for a direct follow. A null value means no route was found within the requested depth in the indexed graph. It does not prove that no connection exists elsewhere on Nostr.
oracleApi.pathCounts: path_count counts shortest directed paths, including when bridges are omitted; counts saturate at the maximum unsigned 64-bit integer. mutual_follow indicates a direct follow in both directions. Optional bridges contains search meeting nodes, not a full path or proof of disjoint paths.
oracleApi.batchDescription: Query up to 100 targets from one source, preserving target order and duplicates.
oracleApi.batchFields: Required JSON fields: from and targets. Optional max_hops, include_bridges and bypass_cache use the same defaults as /distance.
oracleApi.pathDescription: Return intermediate pubkeys on one shortest directed follow path.
oracleApi.pathResult: The example represents two follow edges, from source to bridge to target. Source and target are excluded from path. Self and direct-follow paths return an empty array; no route within the requested depth returns null. This response has no hops field.
oracleApi.followsDescription: Paginate the currently indexed follow list for a pubkey.
oracleApi.unknownPubkey: An unknown pubkey returns an empty list and total: 0.
oracleApi.commonFollowsDescription: Return pubkeys directly followed by both accounts.
oracleApi.mutesDescription: Paginate public pubkey entries from an indexed kind-10000 mute list.
oracleApi.muteListStates: public_list_known: false means no mute-list event was indexed for this pubkey. A known event can have no public pubkey entries, as shown above. Encrypted mute entries are unavailable to the Oracle, and a known empty public list may still contain encrypted entries. Word, hashtag and thread mute tags are excluded from pubkey evidence.
oracleApi.trustDescription: Return follow distance alongside separate public mute observations.
oracleApi.followedMuters: followed_muters lists accounts directly followed by the source whose indexed public mute lists contain the target. The two direct-mute booleans describe the source and target relationship; the known-list flags distinguish missing lists from known public lists.
oracleApi.mutePolicy: Mutes can express personal preference. Missing public evidence is not an endorsement. Clients decide how to use these observations: the response applies no weight, aggregate score or automatic exclusion. Follow distance and mute evidence may be read at slightly different instants during ingestion.
oracleApi.freshnessDescription: sync.coverage is configured_relays_only. Results describe events indexed from the server's configured relays, with no guarantee of global or complete coverage. Cache entries become invalid when the graph revision changes. Neither readiness nor bypassing the cache guarantees that relays have returned the latest event.
oracleApi.profilesUnavailable: Kind-0 profile caching, /profiles and include_profiles are not implemented in v0.3.0.
oracleApi.rateLimits: Data endpoints use a per-IP token bucket configured by RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE. Limits depend on the deployment; requests can be rejected after a burst even before a minute has elapsed. The root, /health and /ready routes are exempt from this limiter. Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB. Do not assume rate-limit headers are present on every response.
oracleApi.errorResponse: Application validation and computation errors return JSON with error and code:
oracleApi.bodyTooLarge: 413: request body exceeds the size limit.
oracleApi.rateLimited: 429: per-IP rate limit exceeded. Back off before retrying; honor retry timing if provided.
oracleApi.unavailable: 503: QUERY_BUSY when query capacity is exhausted, or a readiness snapshot with ready: false from /ready.
oracleApi.retryAdvice: Malformed query strings, malformed JSON and middleware rejections may use a different body format. Check the HTTP status before parsing a successful response. Use bounded retries with backoff for temporary overload.

lnbitsProxy.title: LNbits Provisioning Proxy
lnbitsProxy.intro: A small Node service that sits in front of LNbits and gives Nostr clients a safe, narrow surface for provisioning wallets, claiming Lightning Addresses and managing Nostr Wallet Connect grants. This page is a self-hosting guide: run your own instance against your own LNbits.
lnbitsProxy.whyDescription: LNbits exposes a full administrative API. Handing that to a browser extension would mean trusting every client with instance-wide authority. The proxy publishes only the handful of paths a wallet actually needs, authenticates wallet owners with their Nostr key instead of a password, and keeps the LNbits super-user credential on the server where it belongs.
lnbitsProxy.whyNote: Custom LNbits instances need this adapter for the extension's wallet management UI to work against them. Nothing in the extension is specific to one operator.
lnbitsProxy.architectureDescription: Requests arrive at your reverse proxy over TLS and are forwarded to the service on loopback. The service talks to LNbits over HTTP and reads two LNbits SQLite databases directly for lookups that the HTTP API does not expose.
lnbitsProxy.architectureLoopback: The service binds 127.0.0.1 only. It is never directly reachable from the internet, so a reverse proxy in front of it is required, not optional.
lnbitsProxy.architectureDatabases: Direct database access is how the proxy maps a Nostr public key to an LNbits wallet and how it writes Lightning Address pay links. Both database files must be readable and writable by the user the service runs as.
lnbitsProxy.prerequisitesNode: Node.js 24 or newer. The service uses the built-in SQLite module, which is still experimental on earlier releases.
lnbitsProxy.prerequisitesLnbits: A working LNbits instance with the lnurlp extension installed, and the nwcprovider extension if you want Nostr Wallet Connect support.
lnbitsProxy.prerequisitesBackend: A Lightning backend behind LNbits. The reference deployment uses phoenixd, but the proxy does not care which one you run.
lnbitsProxy.prerequisitesKey: The LNbits super-user API key, which the service uses to create accounts and wallets. This key is never forwarded to clients.
lnbitsProxy.installDescription: Clone the repository, install the single runtime dependency and start the service with its configuration in the environment.
lnbitsProxy.envDescription: Five variables control the service. Only one is required.
lnbitsProxy.envLnbitsUrl: Base URL of your LNbits instance.
lnbitsProxy.envAdminKey: LNbits super-user API key. The service refuses to provision without it.
lnbitsProxy.envDbPath: Path to the main LNbits SQLite database.
lnbitsProxy.envLnurlpPath: Path to the lnurlp extension's SQLite database.
lnbitsProxy.envPort: Loopback port the service listens on.
lnbitsProxy.domainWarningTitle: Change the domain before you deploy
lnbitsProxy.domainWarningBody: The public domain is a constant in the source, not an environment variable. NIP-98 verification rejects any signed event whose u tag does not match it exactly, so an unmodified copy will refuse every provisioning request on your own domain. Edit the constant in server.js to your own hostname before starting the service.
lnbitsProxy.endpointsDescription: Everything the service answers is listed below. Any path not in this list returns 404, including the rest of the LNbits API.
lnbitsProxy.challengeDescription: Issue a single-use random challenge. No authentication. Challenges expire after 60 seconds and are consumed on first successful use.
lnbitsProxy.provisionDescription: Create a wallet for a Nostr public key, or return the existing one. The response carries the wallet's keys and is marked no-store.
lnbitsProxy.provisionBody: Send the signed NIP-98 event as the event field, with an optional wallet name.
lnbitsProxy.claimDescription: Claim a Lightning Address username for the authenticated key. Creates the LNURL pay link and records the username on the account.
lnbitsProxy.lookupDescription: Look up the Lightning Address claimed by a public key. No authentication. The pubkey query parameter is required and must be 64 lowercase hex characters.
lnbitsProxy.releaseDescription: Release a claimed username, freeing it for anyone else and removing the pay link.
lnbitsProxy.nwcDescription: Wallet-scoped management of NWC grants. Every route requires that wallet's Admin API key in the X-Api-Key header; invoice-only keys are rejected. These routes accept no query string at all.
lnbitsProxy.nwcListDescription: List active connections with their budget usage, plus the public provider public key and relay. Returns an empty list if the user has not enabled the extension.
lnbitsProxy.nwcPutDescription: Register a client-generated public key as a connection. A repeat call for the same key is idempotent and returns 200 rather than editing the existing grant.
lnbitsProxy.nwcDeleteDescription: Revoke that wallet's grant for a client public key. Already-dispatched payments are not cancelled.
lnbitsProxy.nwcSecretsNote: The client generates its own secret and builds the pairing string locally. The proxy never receives, stores, logs or returns a pairing secret, and never puts one in a URL.
lnbitsProxy.nwcPermissionsNote: New grants are fixed to pay, lookup and info permissions with a daily budget and an expiry. LNbits remains authoritative for ownership, account restrictions and budget enforcement.
lnbitsProxy.passthroughDescription: Two groups of LNbits paths are forwarded verbatim. Everything else is blocked.
lnbitsProxy.passthroughPublic: Public LNURL paths, forwarded with permissive CORS because wallets call them cross-origin. The Host header is rewritten to your public domain so LNbits builds correct callback URLs.
lnbitsProxy.passthroughWallet: Authenticated wallet paths, which require an X-Api-Key header and are used by the extension's wallet view.
lnbitsProxy.nip98Description: Provisioning and every Lightning Address mutation use challenge-response with a signed Nostr event. There are no passwords and no sessions.
lnbitsProxy.nip98Step2: Build a kind 27235 event carrying the challenge and the exact request it authorizes.
lnbitsProxy.nip98Step3: Sign it with the user's Nostr key and send it as the event field of the POST body.
lnbitsProxy.nip98Step4: The service verifies the Schnorr signature before consuming the challenge, so a failed attempt does not burn it.
lnbitsProxy.nip98TagsDescription: All three tags are mandatory and checked exactly. The u tag must be the full absolute URL of the endpoint being called on your own domain, and the method tag must match the HTTP method.
lnbitsProxy.nip98WindowsDescription: Two independent windows apply: the challenge expires 60 seconds after it is issued, and the event's created_at must be within 60 seconds of server time. A client with a badly skewed clock will fail even with a fresh challenge.
lnbitsProxy.nginxDescription: Terminate TLS and forward to the loopback port. The block below is the reference configuration.
lnbitsProxy.realIpTitle: Set the real client IP if a CDN sits in front
lnbitsProxy.realIpDescription: Rate limiting keys on the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry, which your reverse proxy appends. If a CDN such as Cloudflare proxies your domain, that entry is the CDN's edge address rather than the visitor's, and every user behind the same edge shares one bucket: a handful of requests per minute for everyone at once. Restore the real address before the request reaches the service.
lnbitsProxy.realIpNote: Skip this block only if nothing sits between the internet and your reverse proxy. Keep the address ranges current with your CDN's published list.
lnbitsProxy.processDescription: Any supervisor works. The reference deployment uses pm2, with the configuration injected into the process environment and the process list saved so it survives a reboot.
lnbitsProxy.processEnvNote: Inject the super-user key through your supervisor or an environment file that is never committed. It must not live in the repository.
lnbitsProxy.monitoringDescription: Two independent watchers are worth running: a health check for the stack as a whole, and a watchdog for the Lightning backend.
lnbitsProxy.watchdogDescription: phoenixd can reach a state where the process is alive and listening but its HTTP API never answers, because a reconnect loop to the LSP blocks the event loop. Wallets report failed payments while systemctl reports the service as active. A timer that probes the API and restarts on two consecutive failures recovers this without anyone waking up.
lnbitsProxy.watchdogRetryNote: The double check matters: a single timeout is usually a blip, and restarting the backend on every blip is worse than the fault.
lnbitsProxy.healthDescription: A periodic check that exercises LNbits, the proxy, the public LNURL paths and end-to-end invoice generation, and emails on state changes. Run it from cron on the same host.
lnbitsProxy.healthInvoiceNote: If your check generates real invoices, give it a dedicated wallet and address, use a short expiry, and clean the invoices up. Probing a real user's address every few minutes fills their payment history with invoices nobody ever pays.
lnbitsProxy.rateLimitsDescription: Per client address, per minute. Requests over the limit get 429.
lnbitsProxy.usernameDescription: Usernames must be 3 to 30 characters, lowercase alphanumeric with dots, hyphens and underscores, starting and ending with an alphanumeric character.
lnbitsProxy.nwcLimitsName: Connection name: 1 to 50 characters, no control characters.
lnbitsProxy.nwcLimitsBudget: Daily limit: 1 to 9,999,999 sats, enforced on a rolling 24 hour window.
lnbitsProxy.bodyLimitsDescription: 64 KB for provisioning and Lightning Address requests, 4 KB for NWC connection creation.
lnbitsProxy.sourceDescription: The service is a single Node file with one runtime dependency. Read it before you run it.
lnbitsProxy.envProvisionDb: Pubkey to wallet mapping owned by this service, created automatically.
lnbitsProxy.healthzDescription: Opens both LNbits databases, checks the admin key is configured and pings LNbits. Returns 200 when healthy and 503 with a per-dependency reason otherwise. No authentication.
lnbitsProxy.ownershipDescription: A Nostr public key is resolved to its wallet through the mapping database this service owns. Rows are written only after a NIP-98 signature from that key has been verified.
lnbitsProxy.ownershipMirror: LNbits has its own pubkey column on each account, and the service mirrors into it so the LNbits interface shows the association. It is never read back to decide ownership: LNbits lets any signed-in user set that column on their own account without proving they hold the Nostr key.
lnbitsProxy.ownershipPermissionTitle: Keep the mapping unwritable by LNbits
lnbitsProxy.ownershipPermission: The file permission is what makes wallet ownership trustworthy. Store it outside the LNbits data directory and make sure the user LNbits runs as cannot write it.
lnbitsProxy.ownershipMigrate: On an instance that already has wallets, import the existing mapping before running the new version:
lnbitsProxy.ownershipMigrateNote: The import is idempotent and verifies that every public key still resolves to the same wallet and the same keys as before, exiting with an error otherwise. The deploy script runs it before restarting and stops the deployment if verification fails.
